summary: Registering a GitHub OAuth app is a self-serve process that provides immediate API credentials for user-on-behalf-of actions. The primary complexity involves managing organization-level access, which often requires explicit approval from organization owners.

difficulty.headline: Registration is instant and self-serve, though organization data access may require manual owner approval.

factors.label: Self-Serve Registration
factors.detail: Credentials like the Client ID and Secret are issued immediately upon form submission without a mandatory platform review.

evidence.quote: A registered OAuth application is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret.

factors.label: Organization Restrictions
factors.detail: Access to private organization data is blocked by default if the organization has access restrictions enabled.

evidence.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access

can_test_before_approval.detail: Developers can immediately use their Client ID and Secret to authorize their own account or other users, provided they are not accessing restricted organization data.

evidence.quote: If you want to skip authorizing your app in the standard way, such as when testing your app, you can use the non-web application flow.

requirements.label: Verified Email Address
requirements.detail: The GitHub account owner must have a verified email to authorize or create apps.

requirements.label: Application Name
requirements.detail: A public-facing name for the application.

evidence.quote: In "Application name", type the name of your app.

requirements.label: Homepage URL
requirements.detail: The full URL to your application's website.

evidence.quote: In "Homepage URL", type the full URL to your app's website.

requirements.label: Authorization Callback URL
requirements.detail: The redirect URI where users are sent after authorization.

evidence.quote: In "Authorization callback URL", type the callback URL of your app.

steps.title: Draft App Metadata
steps.detail: Prepare the application name, homepage URL, and a list of up to 10 callback URLs.
steps.agent_assist: Draft a public-facing application name, description, and a list of standard redirect URIs for the developer to copy-paste.

evidence.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs. To add additional callback URLs, click Add callback URL.

steps.title: Navigate to Developer Settings
steps.detail: Access the OAuth app registration area within your GitHub account settings.

evidence.quote: In the left sidebar, click Developer settings.

steps.title: Register the Application
steps.detail: Fill in the application details and click 'Register application' to generate your credentials.
steps.agent_assist: Provide a checklist of required fields (Name, Homepage, Callback) to ensure the developer has all data ready before clicking.

steps.title: Configure Token Expiration
steps.detail: Enable or disable short-lived tokens. GitHub recommends short-lived tokens for better security.
steps.agent_assist: Draft a brief explanation of why expiring tokens (8-hour access, 6-month refresh) are recommended for the agent's security posture.

evidence.quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.

steps.title: Request Organization Approval
steps.detail: If the app needs to access organization data, members must request approval from the organization owner.
steps.agent_assist: Draft a justification message for the organization owner explaining why the app requires access to organization resources.

evidence.quote: Users can request owner approval for OAuth apps they'd like to use, and organization owners receive a notification of pending requests.

gotchas.title: Token Issuance Limits
gotchas.detail: GitHub limits the number of tokens issued per user/app/scope combination; exceeding this revokes older tokens.

evidence.quote: There is a limit of ten tokens that are issued per user/application/scope combination

gotchas.title: Implicit Scope Normalization
gotchas.detail: Requesting a broad scope (like 'user') will automatically include and normalize narrower scopes (like 'user:email').

evidence.quote: the token will be saved with a normalized list of scopes, discarding those that are implicitly included by another requested scope.

gotchas.title: Organization Access Restrictions
gotchas.detail: New organizations have access restrictions enabled by default, blocking unapproved OAuth apps from private data.

evidence.quote: When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default.

blockers.why: Owners can deny any third-party access request to protect organization resources.
blockers.fix: Contact the organization owner directly to discuss the app's security and data requirements.

evidence.quote: When an organization member or outside collaborator requests OAuth app access to organization resources, organization owners can approve or deny the request.

blockers.why: Organizations with SAML enabled require an active session for OAuth authorization to succeed.
blockers.fix: The user must log in to the organization via SAML before attempting to authorize the OAuth app.

evidence.quote: you must have an active SAML session for each organization each time you authorize an OAuth app.

uncertain: The exact duration for organization owner approval as it depends on internal company policies.
Whether the 100-app limit per user/org is strictly enforced or can be increased upon request.
The specific review time for Marketplace listings, though community sources suggest 2-4 weeks.
